hero.headline: Trump considering government equity stakes in major AI companies
hero.teaser: The Trump administration is discussing taking government ownership positions in leading artificial intelligence firms including OpenAI.
hero.body:
President Trump said his administration is exploring the possibility of acquiring equity stakes in leading artificial intelligence companies as a way to generate government profit from the sector's growth.

The proposal would involve direct federal investment in exchange for ownership shares in firms developing advanced AI systems. Trump is scheduled to meet with AI company leaders as soon as next week to discuss the plan, according to reports from multiple news outlets.

The discussions represent a notable shift in how the federal government might approach the rapidly expanding AI industry. By taking equity positions rather than simply regulating the sector, the administration would position itself to benefit financially from the companies' success while maintaining some degree of influence over their operations.

The meetings with OpenAI and other major AI developers mark an unusual convergence of political perspectives. The idea of public ownership stakes in the AI sector has drawn support from across the political spectrum, with both Trump and Senator Bernie Sanders now advocating for forms of government involvement in the industry.

This approach differs from traditional regulatory frameworks that focus on oversight and compliance. Instead, it would make the federal government a direct stakeholder in the financial performance of these companies. The profit-sharing model suggests the administration views AI development as both a strategic priority and a potential revenue source.

The timing of these meetings reflects growing attention to AI's role in the economy and national security. As these companies continue to develop increasingly powerful systems, questions about government involvement have intensified. Some policymakers argue that direct investment would give the government a seat at the table in shaping how these technologies are developed and deployed.

The proposal also raises questions about potential conflicts of interest and the appropriate role of government in private sector investment. Critics might argue that taking equity stakes could compromise regulatory independence, while supporters contend that government participation ensures public interests are protected as the technology advances.

The meetings scheduled for next week will likely provide clarity on which companies the administration is targeting and what specific terms might be under consideration. The discussions could set a precedent for how governments engage with major technology companies going forward.

Both OpenAI and other AI firms will need to evaluate how accepting government investment might affect their operations, governance structures, and ability to operate independently. The outcome of these negotiations could influence the broader landscape of AI development in the United States and shape policy approaches globally.

The convergence of Trump and Sanders around some form of public ownership in AI, despite their general political differences, suggests this issue may have genuine bipartisan appeal among policymakers concerned about ensuring the public benefits from transformative technologies.

cards.headline: US Military Shoots Down Iranian Drones Over Strait of Hormuz
cards.teaser: The US military shot down at least four Iranian drones fired toward the Strait of Hormuz, the Pentagon announced Saturday.
cards.body:
The US military intercepted at least four Iranian drones headed toward the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf allies including Kuwait and Bahrain, according to Pentagon officials. The incident is part of an escalating exchange of military strikes between the United States and Iran in the region.

The Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway carrying roughly one-fifth of global petroleum supplies, has become a flashpoint as tensions between Washington and Tehran intensify. The Trump administration is simultaneously increasing pressure on Iran to reach a deal while military operations continue, even as diplomatic channels remain open.

cards.headline: Stock markets tumble as chip sector selloff drags Nasdaq down 4.2 percent
cards.teaser: US stock markets recorded their worst trading day of the year on Friday, with the Nasdaq composite falling 4.2 percent as investors fled semiconductor and artif.
cards.body:
US stock markets recorded their worst trading day of the year on Friday, with the Nasdaq composite falling 4.2 percent as investors fled semiconductor and artificial intelligence stocks. The S&P 500 dropped 2.6 percent, ending a nine-week streak of gains, while the broader market decline reflected growing concerns about Federal Reserve policy and valuations in the technology sector.

The selloff centered on chip stocks, with the semiconductor sector experiencing what analysts described as a bloodbath. Major technology companies that have driven market gains over the past year saw sharp declines as traders reassessed the sustainability of the artificial intelligence investment boom. The Nasdaq suffered its worst single-day performance since April 2025.

The market turbulence followed a stronger-than-expected jobs report that raised the likelihood of Federal Reserve interest rate increases. Traders increased their bets on Fed rate hikes as the employment data suggested continued economic strength that could keep inflationary pressures elevated. Higher interest rates typically reduce the appeal of technology stocks, whose valuations depend heavily on future earnings growth.

The downturn marked the end of what had been a stellar period for US equities. The week became the worst for stocks since Liberation Day earlier this year, as the combination of rate hike expectations and profit-taking in overextended technology positions prompted widespread selling. Market participants pointed to concerns that artificial intelligence stocks had risen too far too fast without corresponding evidence of revenue growth.

Beyond equities, the risk-off sentiment extended to cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin fell below $60,000 to its lowest level since October 2024, sinking from highs reached during recent geopolitical tensions. The decline suggested investors were rotating away from speculative assets across multiple sectors, favoring safer investments as uncertainty about monetary policy increased.

cards.headline: Putin Rejects Direct Talks With Ukrainian President Zelenskyy
cards.teaser: Russian President Vladimir Putin said he sees no point in meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy over ending the war.
cards.body:
Putin has rejected Zelenskyy's offer for direct talks, calling the Ukrainian president's open letter rude and saying he sees no point in meeting. Speaking at the St. Petersburg economic forum, Putin insisted Russia will achieve its war goals in Ukraine, including seizing the entire Donbas region.

The rejection comes amid escalating tensions, with Ukrainian drone attacks reaching deep into Russian territory. Putin announced Russia will strengthen its air defenses in response to these strikes, which have disrupted his showcase economic forum in his hometown.

cards.headline: Israel Strikes Southern Lebanon After Ordering Village Evacuations
cards.teaser: Israeli forces conducted strikes in southern Lebanon after ordering residents of nine villages to evacuate.
cards.body:
Israel carried out military strikes across southern Lebanon following evacuation orders for nine villages in the region. The offensive has killed thousands and displaced over a million people.

The Israeli military ordered residents to leave towns including Anqoun, which was sheltering at least 2,500 displaced people before the evacuation. Families fled toward Sidon, the nearest major city, as roads became congested with vehicles. Israeli airstrikes, drone strikes, and artillery fire hit multiple areas including Anqoun, the Nabatieh region, and the town of Kfar Tebnit, which sits near Beaufort Castle, a medieval fortress Israeli troops captured this week.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered troops to advance further into southern Lebanon following the castle's seizure. Israel has now issued evacuation orders for Nabatieh, which is normally one of southern Lebanon's largest cities but is now deserted. Israeli forces currently occupy more than 608 square kilometers of Lebanese territory.

The military operations continue despite ceasefire negotiations. A US-brokered ceasefire agreement reached on Wednesday was rejected by Hezbollah on Thursday. The proposed deal would have required Hezbollah to stop firing while allowing Israel to continue airstrikes. Hezbollah characterized this arrangement as "surrender," according to statements from the militant group.

The ceasefire proposal included "pilot zones" where the Israeli military would withdraw from certain areas and Lebanese forces would return to prevent Hezbollah from entering. Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri, who represents Hezbollah's positions in negotiations, criticized this approach. He stated that Hezbollah would only withdraw from areas south of the Litani River, located 18 miles from the Lebanon-Israel border, if Israeli troops completely left Lebanon and if a ceasefire was unconditional.

Netanyahu told cabinet ministers he would not seek government approval for the ceasefire unless Hezbollah agreed first. Some ministers opposed the fragile agreement and wanted a formal cabinet vote, but Netanyahu rejected these demands, saying there was nothing to approve while Hezbollah remained opposed.

Fighting between Hezbollah and Israel began on March 2, following the militant group's rocket attacks on Israel. The conflict has killed more than 3,500 people in Lebanon from Israeli strikes, while Hezbollah operations have killed at least 29 Israeli soldiers and three Israeli civilians in Lebanon.

Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam said Friday that "Lebanon can no longer be a field for wars fought for others, nor can the south and its people continue to pay the price for decisions they did not make."

The ceasefire negotiations involve the US, Israel, and Lebanon, but Hezbollah is not a direct party to the talks. The discussions have wider implications, as Iran has linked success of a Lebanon ceasefire to its own negotiations with Washington.

cards.headline: FDA Investigates Baby Botulism Outbreak, Cause Still Unknown
cards.teaser: Federal regulators continue investigating an outbreak of infant botulism without identifying the source or preventive measures.
cards.body:
The Food and Drug Administration has yet to determine the cause of a baby botulism outbreak or establish guidelines to prevent future cases. The investigation remains ongoing as health officials work to trace the source of the bacterial infection affecting infants.

The three companies involved in the investigation have each attributed responsibility to the others. Botulism in infants typically occurs when babies ingest bacterial spores that produce toxins in the intestinal tract, causing muscle weakness and breathing difficulties.

cards.headline: First advanced nuclear reactor reaches criticality at Idaho laboratory
cards.teaser: A small modular nuclear reactor has achieved criticality for the first time in the United States, marking progress for next-generation nuclear technology.
cards.body:
The Department of Energy announced that a privately developed advanced nuclear reactor called Mark-Zero has reached criticality at Idaho National Laboratory. The milestone represents the first time an advanced small modular reactor has achieved a self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction in the US.

The Antares reactor demonstration at the Idaho facility is part of efforts to develop smaller, more flexible nuclear power systems. Reaching criticality is a critical step in proving the viability of advanced reactor designs that proponents say could provide carbon-free energy with improved safety features compared to traditional large-scale nuclear plants.

cards.headline: Protests Grow Over Jared Kushner Resort Plan in Albania
cards.teaser: Days of protests have erupted in Albania over a luxury resort project linked to Jared Kushner near a protected wetland.
cards.body:
Thousands of demonstrators have taken to the streets of Tirana to oppose a $1.6 billion luxury resort backed by Jared Kushner. The proposed complex is being built in an environmentally sensitive Mediterranean area home to 200 bird species, including flamingos and Dalmatian pelicans. Construction crews have begun erecting concrete fencing with barbed wire around the site, triggering public outrage over environmental damage and concerns about political transparency.

Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama has defended the project, dismissing opposition as politically motivated. Protesters have rallied against the development with slogans including "Albania is not for sale," drawing international attention to the environmental implications of the resort and the involvement of the prominent American political figure in Albanian development.

cards.headline: EU Leaders Signal Montenegro Could Join by 2028
cards.teaser: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Montenegro is within reach of joining the European Union by 2028.
cards.body:
Von der Leyen told leaders at a Western Balkans summit that the EU must demonstrate its capability and willingness to accept new members while making the enlargement process "faster and more credible." German Chancellor Friedrich Merz echoed this sentiment, stating the EU needs to show it can and wants to enlarge.

Von der Leyen indicated that Montenegro is "within reach" of joining by 2028. The summit, held in Tivat, brought together EU leaders and counterparts from six Western Balkan countries seeking membership.

cards.headline: Severe Heat Waves Force Hard Choices for Indian Workers
cards.teaser: Heat waves hitting India since April are forcing essential workers to choose between their health and earning wages.
cards.body:
India has experienced severe heat waves since April, creating difficult conditions for the country's essential workers. Many laborers face the decision of working in dangerous temperatures to earn income or protecting their health by avoiding outdoor work.

The extreme heat particularly affects those whose jobs require them to work outside during the hottest parts of the day. Workers in construction, agriculture, and delivery services are among those most impacted by the prolonged high temperatures. The heat waves represent an ongoing public health and economic challenge as temperatures remain elevated.

cards.headline: France Investigates Alleged Israeli Mistreatment of Gaza Flotilla Activists
cards.teaser: French authorities opened an investigation into alleged abuse of pro-Palestinian activists detained after attempting to reach Gaza by sea.
cards.body:
The investigation follows claims by activists who were detained with a flotilla trying to reach the Gaza Strip. The activists said they were abused while in Israeli custody, allegations that Israeli authorities have denied.

French prosecutors launched the inquiry after receiving complaints from French nationals who participated in the flotilla. The investigation will examine the treatment of the detained activists and whether any laws were violated during their detention by Israeli forces.

hero.headline: Canada bans Texas cattle imports after second screwworm case confirmed
hero.body:
Canada has implemented an import ban on cattle from Texas after a second case of screwworm was confirmed in the state. The discovery prompted Texas to declare a state of disaster as officials work to contain the outbreak.

Screwworm is a parasitic fly larva that burrows into the flesh of warm-blooded animals, including livestock and humans. The parasite can cause severe tissue damage and death without treatment. The United States successfully eradicated screwworm in the 1960s through a sustained campaign, making any reappearance a serious concern for agricultural and public health officials.

The identification of a second infected calf in Texas triggered the state's disaster declaration. This action allows authorities to mobilize additional resources and implement emergency measures to contain the outbreak and prevent further spread. The appearance of a second case suggests the parasite may have established a foothold in the state, raising concerns about broader contamination.

Canada's import ban protects its own cattle industry from the parasite. The restriction will impact Texas ranchers who export cattle across the border, adding economic pressure to an industry already facing containment costs and potential losses. Live cattle trade between the United States and Canada represents a significant portion of cross-border agricultural commerce.

Federal and state veterinary officials are working to determine the source of the infestation and identify how many animals may have been exposed. The response includes quarantines, inspections of nearby herds, and treatment protocols for affected animals. The speed and effectiveness of containment efforts will determine whether the outbreak remains localized or spreads to other parts of Texas and neighboring states.

Screwworm has been absent from the United States for decades due to eradication efforts. Its reappearance in Texas marks a significant development for the livestock industry, which depends on disease-free herds to maintain trade relationships with major trading partners like Canada. The parasite typically enters livestock through open wounds or natural body openings.

The economic consequences of the outbreak extend beyond individual ranchers. Trade restrictions can cascade through the supply chain, affecting processors, exporters, and consumers. Both countries have established protocols for disease management, but the sudden discovery of multiple cases has triggered precautionary measures.

Veterinary teams are collecting samples and conducting epidemiological investigations to understand how the parasite entered Texas. The findings will inform whether additional restrictions are necessary and when trade may resume. Officials anticipate that aggressive containment and treatment efforts will be essential to controlling the outbreak and restoring confidence in Texas cattle exports.

The screwworm outbreak represents a test of cross-border agricultural coordination between the United States and Canada. Both nations maintain strict animal health standards to protect their industries and ensure food safety.

cards.headline: Park ranger dies after falling into crevasse on Mount McKinley
cards.teaser: A National Park Service ranger died after falling into a crevasse on Mount McKinley in Alaska.
cards.body:
A park ranger died after falling into a crevasse on Mount McKinley, the highest peak in North America. The ranger was working on the mountain when the accident occurred.

Mount McKinley, also known by its traditional name Denali, presents extreme hazards including hidden crevasses that can open suddenly in glacial ice. Park rangers routinely work on the mountain to assist climbers and conduct rescue operations in one of the most dangerous climbing environments in the world.

cards.headline: Man who plotted with au pair to kill his wife sentenced to life in prison
cards.teaser: A Virginia man received a life sentence for orchestrating the murder of his wife with the family's au pair.
cards.body:
Brendan Banfield, a former IRS law enforcement officer, was sentenced to life in prison without parole for the murders of his wife Christine and Joseph Ryan. Banfield was having an affair with the family's Brazilian au pair, Juliana Peres Magalhães, who lived with them in Virginia.

Prosecutors alleged that Banfield and Magalhães plotted together to kill Christine, a pediatric intensive care nurse. They lured Ryan to the couple's home on February 24, 2023, as a fall guy for the murder. Banfield claimed he shot Ryan in self-defense after discovering him attacking his wife, but the court rejected this account.

cards.headline: Justice Department argues courts cannot block White House ballroom construction
cards.teaser: Federal lawyers told an appeals court that the president has authority to build a ballroom at the White House without judicial interference.
cards.body:
The Trump administration asked a federal appeals court to overturn a lower court decision blocking construction of a $400 million ballroom at the White House. A Justice Department lawyer argued that no court has authority to halt the project, suggesting only Congress could stop it.

The ballroom would be built on the site of the demolished East Wing. While the legal dispute continues between Washington DC preservationists and the White House, construction of a secure underground bunker at the site was permitted to proceed. The project has grown significantly in both size and cost over the past year.

cards.headline: Iran's World Cup team granted visas to enter United States
cards.teaser: Officials confirmed that the Iranian national football team received approval to enter the United States for the World Cup.
cards.body:
The Iranian football team has been granted visas to enter the United States for the World Cup. The approval was announced just 10 days before Iran's opening match against New Zealand in Los Angeles.

The visa decision marks a significant diplomatic gesture between Washington and Tehran, allowing the Iranian squad to compete in matches scheduled on American soil during the tournament.

cards.headline: Former staffer continues public criticism of Senate candidate Graham Platner
cards.teaser: Genevieve McDonald, who previously worked for Graham Platner, has emerged as a persistent critic of the Senate candidate.
cards.body:
Genevieve McDonald, a former staffer for Graham Platner, has continued to publicly criticize the Senate candidate. McDonald is among several women who have come forward with accounts of unsettling behavior by Platner.

The criticism comes as Platner campaigns for Senate amid what he has characterized as turmoil. Multiple reports have detailed allegations from women who dated or worked with Platner. One accuser called a recent report about Platner's behavior a gift to his campaign, though the remark's intent was unclear from available information.

cards.headline: Senator Brian Schatz offers support for Graham Platner amid allegations
cards.teaser: Hawaii Senator Brian Schatz became the first senator to publicly support Graham Platner despite ongoing allegations.
cards.body:
Senator Brian Schatz has offered the first show of support from the Senate for Graham Platner, who faces multiple allegations. The Hawaii Democrat's backing represents a break from other senators who have remained silent or expressed concern.

Schatz's statement comes as Democrats have expressed worry about Platner's candidacy. The endorsement marks a significant development for Platner, who has been campaigning while addressing reports about his personal conduct.

cards.headline: Google agrees to pay SpaceX nearly $1 billion monthly for cloud computing
cards.teaser: Google has signed a deal to pay SpaceX $920 million per month for computing capacity at data centers operated by xAI.
cards.body:
Google will pay SpaceX $920 million monthly for cloud computing capacity at data centers operated by xAI, Elon Musk's AI company. The multiyear agreement represents one of the largest deals of its kind in the tech industry.

A Google representative attributed the contract to unexpected demand for the company's recently launched AI products. The deal positions SpaceX as a major infrastructure provider for artificial intelligence development alongside its aerospace operations.

cards.headline: States preparing antitrust lawsuit to block Paramount acquisition of Warner Bros
cards.teaser: Multiple US states are planning legal action to prevent the merger between Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery.
cards.body:
A coalition of state attorneys general is preparing to file an antitrust lawsuit challenging Paramount's proposed acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery. The legal action would seek to block the merger on grounds that it would reduce competition in the entertainment industry.

Warner Bros Discovery shares fell on news of the impending legal challenge. Paramount has called the anticipated lawsuit a clumsy attempt to politicize antitrust litigation and is seeking to have any such legal action dismissed. The state-level challenge comes as the merger faces scrutiny over its potential impact on content production and distribution markets.

cards.headline: Bitcoin drops below $60,000 to lowest level since October 2024
cards.teaser: Bitcoin tumbled beneath $60,000 as investors moved away from cryptocurrency amid rate hike expectations and technical issues.
cards.body:
Bitcoin fell below $60,000 for the first time since October 2024, marking a significant decline for the cryptocurrency. Strong employment data fueled expectations for additional Federal Reserve rate increases, pressuring digital assets lower. A technical bug affecting Zcash also contributed to broader concerns about cryptocurrency infrastructure stability.

The sell-off reversed earlier gains bitcoin had made during geopolitical tensions involving Iran. Investors have been shifting away from cryptocurrencies toward traditional equities and artificial intelligence stocks as attention moves to other technology sectors.

cards.headline: Elon Musk leads list of highest-paid chief executives
cards.teaser: Executive compensation is accelerating while rank-and-file worker pay lags, widening the gap in corporate America.
cards.body:
Elon Musk topped the rankings of highest-paid chief executives as executive compensation continues to rise faster than pay for ordinary workers. The data reflects a widening pay disparity between corporate leadership and employees at the same companies.

The compensation figures come as corporate boards have approved increasingly large pay packages for top executives, including stock awards and performance bonuses. The gap between executive and worker pay has become a focus of debate over income inequality and corporate governance practices in American business.

hero.headline: Reid Hoffman Leaves Microsoft Board to Lead AI Drug Discovery Startup
hero.body:
Reid Hoffman has stepped down from Microsoft's board of directors after a decade to focus on Manus, his artificial intelligence drug discovery startup. The LinkedIn co-founder announced his departure to concentrate full-time on the healthcare technology venture.

Hoffman joined Microsoft's board in 2017 following the company's acquisition of LinkedIn for $26.2 billion. During his tenure, he provided strategic guidance as Microsoft expanded its cloud computing business and invested heavily in artificial intelligence partnerships, including its multibillion-dollar collaboration with OpenAI. The board position proved financially rewarding over the past ten years.

Manus represents Hoffman's latest entrepreneurial effort in the intersection of artificial intelligence and biotechnology. The startup applies machine learning and computational methods to accelerate the discovery and development of new pharmaceutical compounds. Drug discovery traditionally requires years of laboratory research and clinical trials, with artificial intelligence promising to reduce timelines and costs by identifying promising molecular candidates more quickly.

The departure reflects a broader trend of technology entrepreneurs returning to hands-on company building after serving in advisory or board roles. Hoffman's move follows recent industry discussions about founders taking more direct operational control of their ventures, sometimes referred to as founder mode. His exit from Microsoft's board eliminates potential conflicts of interest as Manus may compete or partner with major technology companies in the AI space.

Microsoft has not announced Hoffman's replacement on its board. The company continues to pursue aggressive expansion in artificial intelligence applications across its product lines, from cloud services to productivity software. Hoffman's tenure coincided with Microsoft's market capitalization growing to over three trillion dollars, driven largely by its cloud and AI businesses.

cards.headline: International Space Station Crew Returns After Air Leak Repair Attempt
cards.teaser: Astronauts returned to regular operations after sheltering during Russian efforts to fix a persistent air leak in a tunnel section.
cards.body:
Five astronauts aboard the International Space Station have returned to normal duties after being placed on evacuation alert due to an air leak in the Russian segment. NASA ordered the crew to prepare for possible evacuation by entering their docked Crew Dragon spacecraft and donning spacesuits as a precaution.

Russian space officials discovered two air leaks while pressurizing the transfer chamber of the Zvezda module. After the repair attempt was paused, NASA authorized the crew to resume regular activities on Friday morning.

cards.headline: Diver Discovery Solves 20-Year Fish Mystery
cards.teaser: An unusual hairy-looking fish spotted by a diver has resolved a marine biology question that remained unanswered for two decades.
cards.body:
A diver's encounter with an unusual fish covered in hair-like structures has solved a mystery that puzzled researchers for 20 years. The sighting provided the evidence needed to answer longstanding questions about the species.

The fish's distinctive appearance, featuring what looked like hair covering its body, proved key to identifying the specimen. The discovery fills a gap in scientific understanding of the species that had persisted since initial questions arose two decades ago.

cards.headline: Startup Founders Share Negative Experiences With Venture Capitalists
cards.teaser: A widespread social media discussion saw company founders detailing difficult interactions with venture capital investors, with some identifying firms by name.
cards.body:
A viral conversation on X this week featured technology startup founders exchanging stories about their negative experiences with venture capital firms. The discussion gained significant traction, with some founders publicly identifying specific investors and firms involved in their accounts.

The shared anecdotes encompassed a range of problematic behaviors, from unusual requests to situations founders described as infuriating. This public discussion represents an unusual moment of candor in an industry where founders typically avoid openly criticizing potential funding sources.

cards.headline: Guild Wars 3 Announced for PC and PlayStation 5
cards.teaser: ArenaNet revealed the third installment of its massively multiplayer online game franchise at Summer Game Fest, with a beta planned for next year.
cards.body:
ArenaNet announced Guild Wars 3 at Summer Game Fest, bringing the online role-playing game series to PC and PlayStation 5. The developer positioned the title as a modern evolution of the massively multiplayer online genre. A beta test is scheduled for next year.

The game takes place 1,000 years before the events of the original Guild Wars. ArenaNet has not detailed what will happen to Guild Wars 2, which continues to operate with an active player base. The franchise has maintained a following since the first game launched in 2005.

cards.headline: Final Fantasy VII Remake Trilogy to Conclude With Revelation in 2027
cards.teaser: Square Enix revealed the final game in its remake trilogy, set for release in spring 2027 with a new voice actor for a major character.
cards.body:
Square Enix announced Final Fantasy VII: Revelation as the final installment of its remake trilogy, launching in spring 2027 across PC, PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and Nintendo Switch 2. The publisher debuted the first trailer at Summer Game Fest Live, showcasing story and gameplay elements from the concluding chapter.

The trilogy, which began in 2020, will complete its reimagining of the original 1997 PlayStation game with this third full-length release.

hero.headline: Knicks take 2-0 NBA Finals lead with one-point victory over Spurs
hero.body:
The New York Knicks defeated the San Antonio Spurs 105-104 in Game 2 of the NBA Finals on Friday night, securing a commanding 2-0 series lead as the matchup shifts to Madison Square Garden. The Knicks became only the third team in NBA history to win the first two Finals games on the road, joining the 1993 Chicago Bulls and 1995 Houston Rockets.

Playing in San Antonio, the Knicks relied on their star point guard Jalen Brunson to deliver in the final moments. Brunson sank the go-ahead free throw with 9.5 seconds remaining after a crucial turnover by Spurs star Victor Wembanyama. On the final possession, Wembanyama's clean look from the elbow at the buzzer caromed off the back rim, sealing the Knicks' one-point victory.

This marks the second consecutive close game in the series. The Knicks also won Game 1 in a fourth-quarter comeback, overcoming a 14-point deficit in that contest. Brunson has emerged as a key performer in clutch moments throughout New York's playoff run, consistently delivering when games hang in the balance.

The Knicks' success extends beyond these Finals games. New York entered this championship matchup on an 11-game winning streak, dominating opponents throughout their playoff journey. The team now stands just two wins away from capturing their first NBA championship since 1973.

For the Spurs, the loss represents a significant setback. San Antonio had knocked out the defending champion Oklahoma City Thunder in the previous round and entered the Finals with considerable momentum. However, the team struggled to maintain that form on their home court. In Game 1, Wembanyama, widely considered the most exciting player in the NBA, was kept quiet for stretches and shot just 6-of-21 from the field while finishing with 26 points, 12 rebounds and three blocks.

Following Game 2, Wembanyama acknowledged his performance fell short. "I was bad tonight, it's not more complicated than that," he said, dismissing suggestions that the occasion had affected the team's play. "It definitely felt special for sure, but nothing close that could be an excuse."

The Spurs now face an uphill climb. No team in NBA Finals history has overcome a three-game deficit, so winning at least one game in New York is essential to keep their championship hopes alive. The series continues at Madison Square Garden, where the Knicks will look to extend their lead while playing in front of their home crowd. The Spurs must find a way to steal a victory in that hostile environment and bring the series back to San Antonio with momentum on their side.

cards.headline: Iran's soccer team receives US visas for World Cup, support staff denied entry
cards.teaser: Iranian players have been granted entry to the United States for the 2026 World Cup, but many team staff members were denied visas.
cards.body:
Iran's national soccer team has received visas to compete in the 2026 World Cup, which takes place in the United States, Canada, and Mexico. However, many members of the team's support staff were denied entry visas, creating operational challenges ahead of their opening match against New Zealand in Los Angeles.

The visa approvals came just 10 days before Iran's tournament debut, leaving little time for the squad to prepare with a full roster of coaching and support personnel. The decision reflects the complex diplomatic relationship between the two nations, even as the Iranian-American community in Los Angeles prepares to see their national team play on American soil.

cards.headline: England suffers heaviest defeat in 17 years with loss to Spain
cards.teaser: England's national team lost heavily to Spain in their worst defeat since 2009.
cards.body:
England suffered a humiliating 4-0 defeat to Spain in World Cup qualifying, their heaviest loss in 17 years. Goals from Guijarro, Alexia Putellas (twice), and Pina sealed the rout in Mallorca. A one-goal loss would have kept England's hopes of topping their qualifying group alive after an otherwise immaculate campaign, but Spain's emphatic victory has severely damaged their prospects.

The defeat has significant implications for England's World Cup qualification. With head-to-head records set to decide the group if the top two teams finish level on points, Spain now need only beat Iceland on Tuesday to secure first place. England face the prospect of entering qualifying playoffs unless circumstances shift dramatically.

cards.headline: FIFA reverses ban on water bottles at World Cup stadiums
cards.teaser: FIFA changed its policy to allow fans to bring disposable water bottles into World Cup venues after initial backlash.
cards.body:
FIFA reversed its ban on water bottles at World Cup stadiums, now allowing fans to bring disposable bottles into venues. The initial restriction faced public backlash before the governing body changed course ahead of the tournament.

The policy shift comes as the 2026 World Cup prepares to begin next week across North American venues.

cards.headline: Yankees' Aaron Judge diagnosed with rib stress fracture, out 4-6 weeks
cards.teaser: Aaron Judge will be reevaluated in four to six weeks after being diagnosed with a stress fracture in his right rib.
cards.body:
New York Yankees outfielder Aaron Judge received a diagnosis of a rib stress fracture that will sideline him for at least four to six weeks. Judge said the injury initially occurred on a dive in late April, and he attempted to play through the pain before the severity became clear.

The Yankees recalled Spencer Jones to help fill the roster spot. Judge expressed disappointment at having his worst fear realized after trying to continue playing despite discomfort. The injury impacts both the Yankees' playoff positioning and Judge's candidacy for American League MVP honors.

cards.headline: Seattle mayor agrees to activate cameras for World Cup security
cards.teaser: Seattle's mayor reversed her position and agreed to turn on surveillance cameras in the Stadium District during the World Cup.
cards.body:
Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson changed her stance on activating CCTV cameras in the Stadium District, agreeing to turn them on during the FIFA World Cup. The mayor had previously resisted pressure to enable the surveillance system for the tournament.

Critics said Wilson walked the city into an avoidable security situation by delaying the decision. The cameras will now be operational as Seattle prepares to host World Cup matches this summer.

cards.headline: Rangers designate Sam Haggerty for assignment as Corey Seager returns
cards.teaser: The Texas Rangers removed Sam Haggerty from their roster as Corey Seager made his return to the lineup.
cards.body:
The Texas Rangers designated Sam Haggerty for assignment, making room on the roster for the return of shortstop Corey Seager. Seager marked his comeback by hitting a two-run home run in the Rangers' 3-2 victory over the Cleveland Guardians.

Texas rallied late to defeat Cleveland after the Guardians were unable to capitalize on early opportunities. The Rangers improved to 31-32 on the season with the win as Seager's presence immediately impacted the lineup.

hero.headline: Actor James Handy Killed in Tarzana Stabbing, Girlfriend's Son Charged with Murder
hero.body:
Veteran character actor James Handy, 81, died after being stabbed multiple times in the chest at his home in Tarzana, California. He was found unconscious in his front yard at 9:30am on Wednesday and later pronounced dead at the hospital.

Michael Gledhill, 44, the son of Handy's girlfriend, was arrested at the scene and charged with murder. Bail has been set at $2 million. According to police, when officers arrived, Gledhill told them "the one they were looking for." A 911 caller had previously stated: "I am the son of man, I just killed the man of sin." Police confirmed that Gledhill resides at the location with his mother, who is Handy's girlfriend.

Handy built a long career as a character actor spanning multiple decades. He was known for roles in the 2022 blockbuster "Top Gun: Maverick," as well as "Jumanji," "Logan," and "K-911." His television credits include appearances in "Law & Order," "NCIS: Los Angeles," and "Criminal Minds." His career began in 1977 on the television series "Ryan's Hope," and he was born in New York City.

The Los Angeles County District Attorney's Office has emphasized the seriousness of the charges. Murder charges in California carry the possibility of a life sentence. Prosecutors have stated the suspect must be held accountable.

The circumstances that led to the fatal confrontation remain under investigation. Police have not released details about what occurred prior to the stabbing. The case represents a notable loss to the entertainment community, where Handy had become a familiar presence in supporting and featured roles across film and television productions.

This incident adds to a series of violent crimes affecting members of the entertainment industry in the Los Angeles area in recent years. The investigation into the stabbing is ongoing, and Gledhill is being held pending further legal proceedings.

cards.headline: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce Planning July Wedding at Madison Square Garden
cards.teaser: Pop star Taylor Swift and NFL player Travis Kelce are reportedly planning to marry in New York next month.
cards.body:
Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce are planning a July wedding at Madison Square Garden in New York City, according to multiple reports. The couple has reportedly invited over 1,000 guests to the venue for the ceremony. The NYPD commissioner has publicly joked about the rumored event.

Fans have been speculating about when the couple would marry since they began their relationship. The Madison Square Garden venue would represent a high-profile location for what is expected to be one of the most watched celebrity weddings in recent years. Swift is currently one of the world's biggest pop stars, while Kelce plays for an NFL team.

cards.headline: Sean Penn Skipped Oscars for Mental Health, Won Third Academy Award
cards.teaser: Actor Sean Penn won Best Supporting Actor at the Academy Awards but did not attend the ceremony.
cards.body:
Sean Penn won the Best Supporting Actor Oscar at this year's Academy Awards for his role in One Battle After Another, but he was not present at the ceremony to accept the statuette. The actor later revealed he skipped the event for mental health reasons. This marks Penn's third Oscar win in his career.

In a conversation with CNN anchor Kaitlin Collins, Penn explained he will not attend public gatherings with more than eight people and refuses to take selfies with fans under any circumstances. He emphasized this policy applies universally, even declining selfie requests from a Holocaust survivor. The 98th Academy Awards took place without the Best Supporting Actor winner in attendance.

cards.headline: Taylor Swift's Toy Story 5 Song Breaks Streaming Records
cards.teaser: A new Taylor Swift song for the upcoming Toy Story 5 film has set streaming records and received a music video.
cards.body:
Taylor Swift released "I Knew It, I Knew You," a song for Toy Story 5 featuring the cowgirl character Jessie. The track has broken records as the most-streamed country song on Spotify and includes a music video with footage of Joan Cusack's animated character.

The Guardian's review praised the song as Swift's best in years, highlighting its rootsy country sound and handcrafted quality. Swift herself acknowledged the legacy of Randy Newman's iconic Toy Story songs, calling them "incomparable" and crediting Newman with creating the franchise's musical world that she was honored to contribute to.

cards.headline: Rock Tattoo Artist Greg James Dies at 71
cards.teaser: Greg James, a tattoo artist who worked with numerous rock musicians, has died.
cards.body:
Greg James, a tattoo artist known for his work with rock musicians and celebrities, has died at age 71. James had built a reputation as a go-to tattoo artist within the music industry over the course of his career.

James worked with numerous high-profile clients in the rock music world throughout his decades-long career. The cause of death has been reported by media outlets covering the loss of the artist, who was considered legendary within tattoo circles and the music community.

cards.headline: Final Fantasy VII Remake Trilogy to Conclude with Revelation in 2027
cards.teaser: Square Enix revealed the third and final game in its Final Fantasy VII remake series will launch next year.
cards.body:
Square Enix has officially announced Final Fantasy VII: Revelation as the third and final installment in its remake trilogy. The game will release in spring 2027 across PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch 2, Xbox Series X and S, and PC simultaneously.

A first trailer for Revelation debuted at Summer Game Fest Live, showcasing the concluding chapter of Square Enix's reimagining of the classic 1997 RPG. The trilogy's final entry will complete the publisher's multi-game expansion of the original Final Fantasy VII.

cards.headline: Among Us Animated Series Drops on Paramount Plus
cards.teaser: An animated television adaptation of the popular game Among Us is now streaming with all episodes available.
cards.body:
The animated Among Us television show has launched on Paramount Plus with all 10 episodes available immediately. The series stars Yvette Nicole Brown and Liv Hewson, who announced the surprise release at Summer Game Fest in Los Angeles. The show is based on the multiplayer video game that became a cultural phenomenon.

The announcement came as a surprise because there had been limited advance promotion for the series. Among Us became one of the most popular video games in recent years, featuring players working to identify impostors among a crew of characters. The streaming series adapts the game's premise into animated storytelling.

hero.headline: Justice Department ends Trump administration anti-weaponization compensation fund
hero.body:
The Justice Department told a federal court that the Trump administration's nearly $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund will not continue, marking the effective end of the compensation program. Two DOJ attorneys filed the announcement in the Eastern District of Virginia while also requesting the court reject a challenge brought by a former federal prosecutor and several others.

The fund was established to compensate individuals who claimed they were targeted by federal law enforcement for political reasons. The compensation program had become a signature initiative of the Trump administration's efforts to address what it described as politicization of federal agencies.

The court filing provided no explanation for why the administration decided to discontinue the fund. The Justice Department's lawyers combined the announcement with their request to dismiss the legal challenge, suggesting the lawsuit may now be moot given the fund's termination.

The decision affects the nearly $1.8 billion that had been allocated for the program. The former federal prosecutor and other plaintiffs who brought the challenge had contested aspects of how the fund was structured or administered, though details of their specific objections were not provided in available filings.

The anti-weaponization fund represented one of the Trump administration's responses to longstanding complaints from supporters about federal investigations and prosecutions. Its termination signals a policy shift, though the administration has not publicly stated what prompted the change or whether any alternative measures are being considered.

cards.headline: USDA confirms second screwworm case in Texas cattle
cards.teaser: Federal agriculture officials confirmed a second case of flesh-eating screwworm parasite in Texas as they work to contain the outbreak.
cards.body:
The U.S. Department of Agriculture confirmed a second case of New World screwworm in Texas on Friday, detected in a calf in Zavala County. The discovery prompted Texas to declare a state of disaster over the outbreak.

The flesh-eating parasite poses a significant threat to livestock in the region. The outbreak has already triggered international response, with Canada implementing a ban on Texas cattle as the USDA works to contain and eradicate the infestation.

cards.headline: Whistleblower alleges DOGE plan would have marked 2.7 million living people as dead
cards.teaser: A whistleblower claims a plan would have incorrectly marked 2.7 million living people as deceased as part of an immigration enforcement initiative.
cards.body: The alleged plan to mark 2.7 million living people as dead was part of an immigration enforcement push, according to a whistleblower. The disclosure raises concerns about potential impacts on individuals who would have been incorrectly listed as deceased in government records. The whistleblower's allegations suggest the incorrect death designations would have affected millions of people.

cards.headline: Trump discusses price pressures on farmers at rally focused on ending war
cards.teaser: President Trump acknowledged higher fertilizer and fuel prices affecting farmers as supporters cheered for ending the war.
cards.body:
President Trump addressed price increases for fertilizer and fuel that are affecting farmers. The remarks came during a rally where supporters expressed support for ending the ongoing war.

The president also spent considerable time discussing Washington's fountains and the Reflecting Pool during his appearance. Farmers have faced rising input costs that have strained agricultural operations.

cards.headline: Judge orders former CIA officer accused of stealing gold bars to remain jailed
cards.teaser: A federal judge denied release for a former CIA officer facing charges related to allegedly stealing gold bars.
cards.body:
A former CIA official faces theft charges related to allegations involving $40 million in gold bars. Prosecutors have characterized him as a "master manipulator" in connection with the case. The judge has ordered he remain in pretrial detention while the case proceeds.

The defense retains the option to request another hearing should new evidence emerge that supports his release from custody.

cards.headline: Chief of staff for Texas congressman Pete Sessions faces firearm charges
cards.teaser: A top staffer for Rep. Pete Sessions faces multiple firearm charges after allegedly attempting to bring a weapon into the Capitol complex.
cards.body:
Luis Vega, chief of staff for Rep. Pete Sessions, was charged with two counts in connection with an alleged incident days before Christmas last year. The charges stem from allegations that Vega attempted to bring a firearm into the U.S. Capitol complex.

Vega faces several firearm charges filed months after the alleged December incident. The charges were brought against the senior staffer for the Texas Republican congressman in court documents filed this week.

cards.headline: Xavier Becerra wins top spot in California governor race
cards.teaser: Former Health and Human Services Secretary Xavier Becerra clinched the top spot on California's November ballot for governor.
cards.body:
Xavier Becerra secured the top spot on California's November gubernatorial ballot, advancing from a crowded primary field in one of the state's most turbulent campaign seasons. The former Health and Human Services Secretary engineered a come-from-behind victory to lead the race.

With millions of ballots still being counted, Becerra's general election opponent remains to be determined. He could face fellow Democrat Tom Steyer, an environmental activist who has pushed for universal healthcare and taxes on billionaires, or Republican Steve Hilton, a former UK political operative and Fox News personality endorsed by Donald Trump.
